plate_findings.evidence: diffuse lymphoid cell infiltration and a normal epithelium

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H-E of conjunctival biopsy in conjunctival lymphoma case report showing diffuse subepithelial lymphoid infiltration with normal epithelium, matching marginal zone lymphoid infiltrate. B: Higher-power H-E view of same conjunctival biopsy showing diffuse lymphoid infiltration beneath normal epithelium in conjunctival lymphoma case. C: H-E showing dense diffuse subepithelial lymphocytic-like proliferation with normal epithelium, consistent with conjunctival lymphoma marginal zone infiltrate. D: High-power H-E showing monotonous small lymphoid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei without germinal centers beneath normal epithelium, classic for conjunctival lymphoma.

in_text_mentions: unctiva was pulled to observe where the most infiltrated area was, then xylin was injected under it. The conjunctival epithelium and subepithelial tissue from the area with a modified appearance were cut out and then sutured with 7.0 thread. Histopathological examination of the tissue sections with hematoxylin-eosin (H-E) staining revealed: diffuse subepithelial cellular proliferation, with lymphocytic-like cells (small-sized cells with hyperchromatic nuclei, with a relatively uniform appearance, without the formation of germinal centers, reduced cytoplasm) and a normal epithelium (Fig. 2A-D).
